subject: Dedicated capacity: traffic deconvolution + SLA mapping
messages:
From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@lumina.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@lumina.ai
Date: 2028-04-11T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Sizing for Dedicated - quick traffic snapshot

Hey Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Redwood's routing and caching approach looks promising for our multi-tenant inference needs. We want to get a tighter thumbprint for dedicated capacity before the procurement kick-off.

I've attached a CSV with three weeks of real production logs (anonymized): request_timestamp, model_variant, prompt_len, completion_len, latency_ms, customer_tier. A few things to call out up front:
- 10% of requests are long-form generation (prompt > 1.5k tokens, avg completion ~2k tokens)
- 60% are short Q&A (prompt < 200 tokens, completion < 150 tokens)
- We have two priority tiers: "interactive" (p95 latency target 250ms) and "batch/async" (p95 target 1200ms)

Primary asks:
1) Can you map this traffic into an initial GPU pool footprint and a recommended burst policy?
2) What assumptions would you make for KV cache hit-rate and prefix reuse for long-form customers?
3) Any immediate red flags for our latency SLOs given the mix?

If it helps, I'm happy to hop on a 30-min call with engineering this week.

—Alex
CTO, Lumina AI

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@lumina.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-11T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated - quick traffic snapshot

Alex — thanks for the data and context. High level notes after a quick skim:
- The long-form tail will dominate GPU-hours if served naively; we should quantify the long-run average tokens/sec and then apply quantization + batching to bound cost.
- Interactive tier requires aggressive KV cache usage and small-batch low-latency paths. We'll likely split the pool by routing policy: latency-optimized (smaller batch, higher e2e guaranteed throughput) + throughput-optimized (larger batch, lower cost).

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa: can you run a traffic deconvolution template on their sample and produce a histogram of prompt+completion length buckets, plus concurrency curves by hour? (I attached the template we use.)
- Vivek: can you prepare a first-pass GPU SKU mapping (A100xlg / H100 / 8-bit quant variants) and an estimated token throughput per GPU for their mix?

Alex — can you confirm whether the "interactive" tier is latency-sensitive across all customers or only a subset (they tag a customer_tier in the CSV)? Also, any contractual minimums for warm-up windows or cold-start penalties?

Happy to schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow after our eng triage.

Best,
Aditya
Head of Pre-Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-12T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated - quick traffic snapshot

Attachment: lumina_traffic_sample_v2.csv

Folks — I ran the deconvolution template and pulled a few quick artifacts (attached CSV + a short notes PDF). Highlights:
- Prompt+completion length buckets (approx):
  * tiny: <128 tokens — 42% of requests (median latency ~80ms in streaming optimized path)
  * small: 128-512 tokens — 28%
  * medium: 512-1500 tokens — 15%
  * long: >1500 tokens — 15% (but these represent ~48% of total token volume)
- Concurrency profile: 99th percentile concurrent requests peaks at ~1.9k across regions during business hours; 50th percentile ~420.
- Prefix reuse / caching: estimated prefix reuse around 18% (by identical prompt fingerprints) for the interactive tier, slightly higher for small templates.

Quick recommendations for a first-pass dedicated pool:
- Baseline pool: 8 H100s (48GB) configured in two sub-pools: 5 for latency-optimized (p95 target 250ms) and 3 for throughput work. This assumes radix batching + token-parallel quantized kernels and an overall cache hit-rate improvement to 30% after we enable prefix caching.
- Burst policy: add burst capacity of up to +50% via shared burst reservation (pay-as-you-go) with automated fallback to the throughput pool on sustained load.
- Expected monthly token hours (approx): 145k token-hours (subject to quantization gains).

I put detailed per-bucket token/sec numbers in the spreadsheet. Priyom — can you take these and produce a simple SKU + cost delta table?

-M

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@lumina.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-13T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated - quick traffic snapshot

Alex / team — adding the SKU map and conservative throughput numbers inline:

Assumptions: 8 GPUs baseline (5 latency, 3 throughput)
- H100 (80GB) - latency path - effective throughput: ~750K tokens/sec per GPU for small tokens with 8-bit quantized kernels
- H100 (80GB) - throughput path - effective throughput: ~1.2M tokens/sec per GPU for larger batch jobs
- A100 40GB (if customer prefers) - 20-30% lower tokens/sec in latency path vs H100

Cost/ops notes: thermal headroom and KV cache memory for long-form sessions require steady-state local NVMe caching on the latency pool or a warmed distributed cache; without that we saw a 35% p95 latency uplift in tests.

I'll prepare a concise slide with three sizing options (conservative / baseline / aggressive) for the commercial team to include in the proposal.

—Vivek

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@lumina.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-14T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated - traffic deconvolution + SLA mapping (next steps)

Great progress — thanks everyone. Alex, next steps from our side:
- We will produce a 1-page capacity plan (Conservative / Baseline / Aggressive) by EOD Friday with clear assumptions on quantization, cache hit-rate improvements, and burst profile.
- Commercial will include a mutually-agreed uptime SLA and a canary rollout plan (2-week ramp with traffic shadowing).
- Please confirm procurement timelines (we assume a 60-day lead time for dedicated pool provisioning unless you request expedited capacity) and whether Lumina needs a private deployment (VPC) or hosted dedicated.

I've attached a mutual action plan template (RDM-MAP-README.pdf) and our recommended drive folder for artifacts. If the procurement contact wants to be looped in, please add them to replies.

Thanks — I'll slot a 30-min review for Monday to walk the capacity plan.

Aditya
Head of Pre-Sales, Redwood Inference
